title: [Devlog] From AI Concept to a Flyable Ship in 5 Mins — Adding 3D AI models to my Three.js Multiplayer Game (Sidera Caeli)
author: danidomen
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I’ve been working (with a great help of different AIs) on **Sidera Caeli**, a web-based multiplayer space game built with **Three.js**, for about a month now. In this quick video, I wanted to show how fast the pipeline is for adding new content to the game using AI generation tools.

**The Workflow:**

1. **Concept:** Generated a initial ship concept with ChatGPT.
2. **3D Mesh:** Converted the idea into a 3D model using **MeshyAI** and **Tripo3D**.
3. **Quick Cleanup:** Opened it in **Blender** just to clear out the cockpit windows so the interior is transparent.
4. **Integration & LODs:** Imported the chassis directly into the Sidera Caeli custom web editor, positioned the components, and ran it through an auto-LOD system for performance optimization.
5. **Flight Test:** Took it out of the hangar and flew it down to a procedurally generated planet ("New Recipe 2") using my custom planetary system, **TerraForm**, which handles biome rendering and dynamic tree/rock scattering.

Is it AAA release quality? Of course not—there are plenty of camera tweaks and visual polish steps left, and everything is very much a *work in progress*. But being able to go from a text prompt to a fully flyable multiplayer asset in under 5 minutes inside a web browser is super exciting for rapid prototyping!
